title: AI Product Video Generator for Demos | AIVideosUGC
description: Our AI product video generator shows your item in action, from a lid clicking shut to a lamp switching on. Make a short demo for Etsy, Shopify, or your ads.
h1: AI Product Video Generator for Showing How It Works
lead: Our AI product video generator shows what your product does, not just what it looks like. Describe one action, add a photo, and get a short demo clip for your product page, Etsy listing, or ads.
intro: A product demo shows the item doing its job. The kettle pours, the folding chair snaps open, the drawer organizer fills up with spoons and forks. Shoppers can't hold your product, so a few seconds of it in use answers questions a photo can't, like how big it looks in a hand or how the lid comes off.

With AIVideosUGC, you upload a product photo and describe one action in a sentence. Clips run 6, 10, or 15 seconds and come wide 16:9 for a product page, square for listings and feeds, or vertical for Shorts. It works well for home goods, kitchen tools, gadgets, and bags, where the way something moves or opens is part of the appeal. Keep each video to a single action, and make another one for the next feature.

benefits.d: A short clip of the lid opening or the light turning on explains more quickly than a list of specs.
Focused clips are easier to watch and easier to reuse. Make one for each feature and place them where they fit.
Choose 16:9 for a product page, 1:1 for listings, or 9:16 for YouTube Shorts, all from the same photo.

steps.t: Add a photo of the product
steps.d: Use a photo that shows the part that moves or opens, so the video has the right detail to work with.
Write what happens, such as “the lunch box lid clicks shut and the latch locks.” Then pick a size and 6, 10, or 15 seconds.

steps.t: Save it or show another feature
steps.d: Download the clip, then write a new action to make a separate video for the next feature.

uses.d: Etsy listings can show a short video alongside your photos, and a 6 to 15 second clip fits that slot.
Place a wide or square demo with your product photos so shoppers see it work before they buy.
Post a vertical cut that shows one feature to reach people browsing Shorts.
If your seller account can add videos to listings, a short demo can sit next to your images.

faq.q: How is this different from image to video?
faq.a: Image to video adds camera movement to a photo you already have and keeps its look. A product video shows the item being used, like a zipper opening or a pump being pressed, so the scene can change more.

faq.q: Can I use the video on Etsy or Shopify?
faq.a: Yes. Etsy accepts short listing videos with your photos, and Shopify lets you add video to product media. Download the clip and upload it much like you'd add a photo.

faq.q: Will the video show my product accurately?
faq.a: Only describe actions your product can really do, and watch the clip before posting. If a button, color, or part looks different from the real item, make a new version rather than using that one.

faq.q: Can I add the price and product name?
faq.a: Add text later in Canva or CapCut. Letters generated by AI can come out garbled, so typed text is more reliable for names, prices, and dates.
